name: Exemestane (aromatase inhibitor endocrine therapy)
histology: hormone-receptor-positive invasive breast carcinoma (histology-agnostic; includes invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC))

biomarkers.note: Endocrine therapy REQUIRES hormone-receptor-positive disease (ER and/or PR positive). Exemestane is a steroidal aromatase inhibitor (aromatase inactivator) and works only in a low-estrogen (postmenopausal) environment: it is used in postmenopausal patients, or in premenopausal patients ONLY with concurrent ovarian function suppression/ablation (exemestane plus ovarian suppression was a SOFT/TEXT arm). HER2 is tested to guide added HER2-directed therapy and does not change the endocrine indication. Per DeVita 12th ed. (Chapter 16) and Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer, Principles of Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy (BINV-K).

lineOfTherapy: adjuvant endocrine therapy (curative-intent early breast cancer, including with ovarian suppression per SOFT/TEXT) and endocrine therapy for ER- and/or PR-positive metastatic disease; not cytotoxic-line-scoped

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: hormone-receptor-positive (ER and/or PR positive) breast cancer
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer / DeVita 12th ed.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K; DeVita lines 30190 to 30194 (metastatic and adjuvant settings)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: postmenopausal (natural or induced); in premenopausal patients only with concurrent ovarian function suppression/ablation (exemestane + OFS per SOFT/TEXT)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Invasive Breast Cancer / DeVita 12th ed.
eligibilityCriteria.locator: NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K 2 of 4 (5 y of OFS optimal; SOFT OFS + exemestane) and 3 of 4; DeVita lines 185051 to 185084

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: not recommended as monotherapy in male breast cancer (tamoxifen is the male endocrine standard; if an aromatase inhibitor is used in men it requires concurrent GnRH agonist)

drugs.name: Exemestane

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 30205 and 30208 (FDA-approved dose 25 mg per day; administered once daily by mouth, recommended daily dose 25 mg)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. lines 30205 and 30208. Exemestane 25 mg by mouth once daily, continuous (flat daily dosing; the days array marks once-daily administration within a nominal 1-day cycle). Steroidal aromatase inhibitor (irreversible aromatase inactivator). Adjuvant duration 5 years, with extended aromatase inhibitor duration (7.5 to 10 years total) considered for node-positive disease (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K).

regimen.cycles: continuous once-daily dosing for 5 years (adjuvant), extended to 7.5 to 10 years total may be considered for node-positive disease; continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity in metastatic disease
supportiveCare: Not myelosuppressive; no G-CSF or routine antiemetics required (oral endocrine therapy).

Ovarian suppression (OFS) is MANDATORY when used in premenopausal patients: GnRH agonist (e.g., goserelin 3.6 mg SC every 4 weeks) or surgical/radiation ablation; exemestane plus OFS was a SOFT/TEXT regimen. Per NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K 2 of 4 and 3 of 4; DeVita lines 185051 to 185084.

Bone health: aromatase inhibitors increase fracture risk and cause bone loss; monitor bone mineral density and consider a bisphosphonate or denosumab plus calcium/vitamin D (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K footnote q).
Arthralgia/myalgia and steroidal-type effects (weak androgenic properties at higher doses) may occur (DeVita lines 30196 to 30204).

monitoring: adherence to daily oral endocrine therapy (crucial to outcome)
bone mineral density (baseline and periodic) given fracture risk
in premenopausal patients on OFS: confirm ongoing postmenopausal-range estradiol; vaginal bleeding on an AI warrants urgent review
clearanceChecks: postmenopausal status confirmed (or OFS in place for premenopausal)

doseModificationRules.text: Options include switching to another aromatase inhibitor after a washout, or to tamoxifen; supportive measures include exercise, NSAIDs, or duloxetine (NCCN v6.2026 supportive-care discussion; DeVita lines 30196 to 30204). Physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Chapter 16 exemestane: dose lines 30205 and 30208; pharmacology/mechanism lines 30186 to 30214; toxicity lines 30196 to 30204; premenopausal OFS-plus-exemestane (SOFT/TEXT) lines 185051 to 185084; metastatic endocrine therapy lines 186178 to 186209; male breast cancer lines 185885 to 185890

guideline.locator: Principles of Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy (BINV-K 4 of 4: Postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor 5 y, category 1; BINV-K 3 of 4 and 2 of 4: Premenopausal aromatase inhibitor + ovarian suppression/ablation, 5 y OFS optimal per SOFT/TEXT with OFS + exemestane; footnote g: anastrozole/exemestane/letrozole similar efficacy and extended AI 7.5 to 10 y for node involvement; footnote q: bone-density support)

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for exemestane (steroidal aromatase inhibitor / aromatase inactivator) endocrine therapy. Restricted to hormone-receptor-positive (ER and/or PR positive) breast cancer; histology-agnostic across invasive ductal (#1) and invasive lobular (#2) carcinoma. Dose is flat daily oral: exemestane 25 mg by mouth once daily, sourced to DeVita 12th ed. lines 30205 and 30208 (recommended daily dose 25 mg, administered once daily by mouth). Used in postmenopausal patients, or in premenopausal patients ONLY with concurrent ovarian function suppression/ablation (exemestane plus OFS was a SOFT/TEXT arm; DeVita 185051 to 185084). Adjuvant duration 5 years, extended to 7.5 to 10 years total considered for node-positive disease (NCCN v6.2026 BINV-K footnote g). Not recommended as monotherapy in male breast cancer (DeVita 185885 to 185890). Bone-health monitoring and support advised. No ISMP tall-man agent. No field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
